title: Reverse the Order of the Words
statement: `text` contains words separated by spaces; there may be **extra spaces** at the start, at the end and between words. Return the words in **reverse order**, joined by **exactly one space**, with no space at the start or the end. The letters inside each word keep their order.
constraints: text contains lowercase letters and spaces

examples.explanation: The extra spaces disappear and the four words come out in reverse order.
One word stays as it is.

hints.nudge: First split the text into words, ignoring empty pieces. Then you only need to reverse a list.
hints.pattern: Split on whitespace (dropping empty pieces), reverse the list of words and join with one space. Or scan from the end of the text and copy the words.
hints.pseudocode:
words = pieces of text between spaces, skipping empty pieces
reverse words
return words joined by one space
hints.walkthrough: Many languages have a split that treats runs of spaces as one separator; if yours does not, split on single spaces and throw away the empty pieces that extra spaces produce. Reverse the list and join it with one space; an empty list joins to the empty text. Without library helpers you can scan the text from the right: skip spaces, find the end of a word, copy it, add one space between words. O(n) time, O(n) memory.
